title: Packing, costing and selling your soap

say: Welcome to Packaging, Costing and Selling Your Soap, module 4 of our soap making course.
A good bar only becomes income when it is packed well, priced from real costs, and sold to customers who come back.
Look at these bars on the rack. Only pack soap that has finished drying or curing and has passed its tests.
Wrapped wet soap can sweat, soften or grow spots inside the wrapper.

shots.label: Shrink film and paper band
say: Watch the wrapping. Each bar goes into shrink film with a little space at the ends, the ends are sealed, then the printed band goes on with the batch code.
Laundry bars sell in wrappers and in cartons of 12 or 24. Bath bars look best in a paper box or kraft wrap that lets them breathe.

card.title: Ada Clean laundry wrapper
rows: Keep out of reach of children
card.note: Chinyere's label, from the course worked example

shots.banner: No NAFDAC number until you are given one
say: Here is Chinyere's laundry wrapper. Her bars dry to an average of 186 g, so she prints 180 g, a little below, so every bar meets the label.
The batch code LB-2610-07 means laundry bar, year 2026, month 10, seventh batch that month. If a customer complains, it leads you straight to the batch sheet.
Add her name, phone number and caution line. And never print a NAFDAC number you have not been given.
Store wrapped bars in cartons in a cool, dry, shaded room, off the floor.
Keep laundry and bath stock apart so scents don't transfer, and keep all soap away from caustic soda, fuel and food. Sell the oldest batches first.

card.title: 10 kg run cost sheet (example)
card.note: Illustrative prices; use your own receipts

say: Now the money. Many makers count only oil and caustic soda, then wonder why there is no money left.
Chinyere's sheet also counts water, gas, wrappers, labour and a share of rent and transport. The total is 42,540 naira.
These prices are examples only. Replace every figure with your own receipts.

card.title: From cost to price
card.note: 73 good bars, from the course worked example

say: Divide the total by the good bars: 42,540 divided by 73 is 583 naira per bar. That is her floor price.
She sells wholesale at 750 naira and retail at 900. If she sells 48 bars wholesale and 25 retail, the run earns 15,960 naira after paying her helpers.
Rerun the sheet whenever prices move. If PKO rises from 2,600 to 3,000 naira per kg, her cost per bar rises from 583 to 621 naira.
Equipment of 150,000 naira, at 15,960 profit per run, takes about 10 runs to pay back. And count your own time as labour, even if you work alone.

card.title: Wholesale price ladder
card.note: Every step stays above the 583 naira cost

shots.banner: Never sell below your cost per bar
say: Bulk buyers expect a better price, so write a price ladder and share it as a picture.
A laundry business orders 5 cartons every two weeks at 720 naira a bar. That is 43,200 naira per order, and every bar still makes a profit.
Who buys? Market traders want cartons of laundry bars. Laundries and dry cleaners want hard bars and powder in bulk. Schools and hostels need regular deliveries.
Salons, small hotels and event planners buy bath bars and gift soaps. Visit with samples and a printed price list.

shots.banner: Confirm payment in your own account
say: Take orders on WhatsApp Business with a catalogue of real photos of your bars.
Before you release goods, confirm the money has arrived in your own bank account or app. Screenshots can be faked.
Keep an order book: customer, product, quantity, price, date paid and date delivered.
When a complaint comes, write down the batch code on the wrapper, find the batch sheet and your retained samples, and test them.
If the fault is yours, replace or refund promptly and fix the cause. Handled openly, complaints build trust.
Grow step by step: every batch passing its tests, then two or three steady bulk buyers, then bigger runs. Register your business name with CAC and start NAFDAC registration before supermarkets.
Now go through the lessons below, and do the practice task: fill in your own cost sheet and write your price ladder.
